skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: The warning at T2 came right after the witness's opening at T1 and said counsel represents the Committee and the company, not the witness personally, and cannot give legal advice. It did not state the purpose of the interview or the duty to be truthful.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 says the privilege belongs to the company and the company may decide to share what the witness says, including with the government. The witness confirmed the point at T3.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: The interviewer never explained how the interview would run, asked the witness to flag speculation, or distinguished recollection from uncertainty. The only invitation was the open prompts later in the interview.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 ended with 'Any questions?' and the witness said 'That's clear' at T3. The witness then said they might want their own counsel, and the interviewer did not address that.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: At T154 the interviewer asked if there was anything else the Committee should know, and at T156-T158 asked about other witnesses and documents. At T162 the interviewer gave a confidentiality and record-keeping reminder, but did not state explicit next steps.

moments.text: We represent the Committee and the company, not you personally. We're not your attorney and can't give you legal advice.
the privilege belongs to the company, and the company may decide to share what you tell us with others, including the government.
I understand you're not my lawyer.

The warning covered the company as client, the lack of personal representation, privilege and disclosure, and ended with 'Any questions?'. It did not explain how the interview would proceed or ask the witness to flag speculation.
Is there anything I haven't asked about that you think the Committee should know?
Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?
Please keep any documents related to this, and don't discuss this interview with anyone.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Each new topic opened with a broad invitation such as 'Tell me everything you remember' at T12, T32 and T46, and the witness was allowed to walk through events before narrower questions.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The interview moved from role and reporting lines (T4-T11) to LJM1, Rhythms, Chewco, LJM2 and 2001 payments, narrowing within each topic. The order was sensible throughout.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions were single and clear, such as T14 and T88. Some were loaded, such as T130 'How did it go from about $1 million to about $10 million?', which assumed a fact.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The tone stayed polite and controlled, and the interviewer did not argue with the witness. Some framing, such as 'How does a $4.5 million return fit with that?' at T82, was pointed but not hostile.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer changed course when answers called for it, for example pressing on the Fastow Family Foundation at T70 after the witness hedged at T69 and T71. Other openings, such as T41 'I believe he told the Board', were left unexplored.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Tell me everything you remember about the controls put in place when the Board approved LJM2 in October 1999.
What did Mr. Causey and Mr. Buy actually review before they signed its approval sheet?
What investments connected to LJM1 did the foundation make in early 2000?
Help me understand the difference.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: The interviewer followed up on evasive answers, including the 'various considerations' at T37-T38, the 'few hours a week' at T107-T109, and the Chewco denial against the 'Andy' note at T136. Some responses such as 'I may have mentioned it to him' at T97 were not followed up.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interview covered who (Kopper, Glisan, Causey), what (the structures), when (dates such as March 2000 and September 2001), and how (approvals and negotiation) across most topics.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: When the witness said 'I'd have to look at the sheet' at T53 or 'I'd have to check' at T79, the interviewer did not offer the approval sheet or other records. Documents were used later, at T72, T98 and T132, but not as a systematic way to refresh memory.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer did not ask how the witness knew secondhand points, such as Skilling telling the Board at T41 or the Chewco buyout terms at T125. The witness's personal role was separated only partly, through T84-T89.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: At T156 the interviewer asked who else to speak with, and the witness named Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, Andersen and V&E at T157.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: At T158 and T160 the interviewer asked about deal files and the witness's personal notes and emails about LJM, Chewco and Southampton, and the witness identified the approval sheets and partnership agreements.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked 'How far above, on the best of them?' at T64, but did not test the hedged answers such as 'I believe so, yes' at T43 or 'I don't recall it coming up specifically' at T45.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Material answers were followed up, such as the Raptor returns at T63-T64, the counsel's doubts at T145-T146, and the Southampton terms at T88-T89. Some answers, such as T149 'I may have said it should be resolved', were left unclear.

moments.text: How far above, on the best of them?
About three hours a week, I believe.
The interviewer asked the witness to reconcile the earlier claim of staying out of the Chewco buyout with the 'Andy' note referring to $10.5 million.
Did they tell you there was no basis for the payment?
The witness said 'I'd have to look at the sheet' about approval timing, and the interviewer did not put the approval sheet in front of the witness.
The witness said Skilling approved Chewco and 'I believe he told the Board', and the interviewer did not ask how the witness knew or what records exist.
The witness said 'I don't recall it coming up specifically' about the November 5 call and was not pressed to test that memory.
The witness said 'I may have mentioned it to him' about inviting Glisan to Southampton, and the interviewer did not follow up.
Do you have any personal files, notes, or emails about LJM, Chewco, or Southampton?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: The Southampton agreement, the LJM2 report and the Kopper note were relevant and introduced after eliciting the witness's memory. The payroll email at T150 had no connection to the matter and was not contextualized.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: Before each document the interviewer first asked open questions, such as the Foundation's activities at T69-T70 before the Southampton agreement at T72, and the returns at T58-T65 before the LJM2 report at T98.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: The descriptions matched the documents: the Foundation's $25,000 contribution at T74, the 193, 278 and 2,500 percent returns at T100, the $10.5 million figure in the note at T132, and the roughly $4.5 million distribution at T80.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: Most framing asked the witness to reconcile the documents, such as 'Help me understand how those fit together' at T136, but some questions leaned toward a conclusion, such as 'How does a $4.5 million return fit with that?' at T82.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: The interviewer gave the witness room to explain inconsistencies, for example at T83, T102-T103, T116-T117 and T136-T137, and did not cut off the explanations.

moments.text: I'd like to show you the Southampton Place partnership agreement, dated March 20, 2000.
It lists a $25,000 contribution from the Fastow Family Foundation. Is that the investment you mentioned a moment ago?
Our information is that on May 1, 2000, about six weeks after it invested, the Foundation received roughly $4.5 million on its $25,000. Is that accurate?
It lists returns of 193, 278, and 2,500 percent on the Raptor transactions, against the roughly 30 percent the Board was shown.
Here is a handwritten note from Mr. Kopper, addressed to 'Andy,' that refers to $10.5 million for the Chewco buyout.
I'd like to show you an email from Enron Payroll Services dated November 2, 2001, about direct deposit changes. Do you recognize it?

missed_opportunities: T45: After the witness said 'I believe so, yes' about being on the November 5, 1997 call (T43) and then 'I don't recall it coming up specifically' about Kopper's role (T45), the interviewer did not ask who else on the call would remember or what the minutes show. That was a chance to test certainty and find another source.

T97: The witness said 'I may have mentioned it to him' when asked who invited Glisan to Southampton. The interviewer did not ask what was said or when, even though the earlier Kopper and Fastow pitches were a live issue.
tips: When you say you believe Mr. Skilling told the Board, what did you personally see or hear, and who else in that room would know?
Before we leave this topic, what exactly did you say to Mr. Causey after that counsel call, and what would your notes or emails show about it?
